guards.what: Rip (BrainLeech.cs:51-61): 5 damage, then RewardCount iterations of a 3-card COLORLESS CardReward offered through RewardsCmd.OfferCustom -- a SKIPPABLE screen
guards.issue: events/brain_leech.py:53-67 takes the damage and builds the same 3-card colourless choice with the same flags (NoRarityModification|NoCardPoolModifications -> mutate_pity=False, modify_hooks=False), but then does `for card in self.run.select_cards('card_reward', cards, 1): add_card(card)`, and select_cards always returns a card when the candidate list is non-empty (run.py:384-390). The player cannot decline the card. That is observable: the colourless pool contains curses and situational cards, and BrainLeech's own SHARE_KNOWLEDGE branch shows the source distinguishes the two screens deliberately -- it sets `Cancelable = false` there and uses plain OfferCustom here. Unlike the Battleworn Dummy potion case there is no driver-level skip to fall back on: the card is added inside the event. LIVE -- Brain Leech is eligible in acts 1-2 with no other gate.

guards.what: EV-1: Rip's 5 HP loss (BrainLeech.cs:53) can reduce the player to 0 HP. C# routes event damage through CreatureCmd.Damage, whose Hook.ShouldDie / Hook.AfterPreventingDeath pass runs over RunState.IterateHookListeners (RunState.cs:545-596), which yields the POTION BELT outside combat; RunState.lose_hp (run.py:294-302) just subtracts
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-1, one verdict at all 18 lose_hp sites (rule 3). Fairy in a Bottle (FairyInABottle.cs:33-45: ShouldDie false for its owner, AfterPreventingDeath heals to max(MaxHp*0.3, 1)) IS ported (potions.py:1222-1250) and IS in the reward pool (potion_pools.py:49), but the sim's copy returns early when `self.combat is None` (potions.py:1246-1248) and is only registered as a listener by CombatState (combat.py:164-166), so it is inert during an event. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py lethal`): a run at 5 HP holding a belt Fairy that loses 15 HP ends DEAD at hp=-10 with the Fairy still in the belt; the game ends alive at 24 HP with the Fairy consumed. LIVE -- both sides ported and reachable, and the divergence ends the run. Secondary: run.lose_hp does not clamp at 0 either, so the sim carries negative HP.
